title: Resumable stream decoder: preserving toolcall boundaries and escape semantics on partial/truncated JSON
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a robust, resumable stream decoding strategy for structured JSON payloads emitted by models in streaming mode. Goals: (1) guarantee tool/function call boundary preservation even when the connection truncates mid-token or mid-escape sequence, (2) provide deterministic heuristics for resuming from a checkpoint without introducing duplicate or malformed tool calls, and (3) minimize customer-visible failures and retries while preserving developer ergonomics for downstream tool consumers.
background: Current streaming decoder uses simple delimiter heuristics that fail on truncated escape sequences (e.g., broken Unicode escapes, unfinished string escapes like '\u' or '\n' in progress) and when toolcall markers are split across fragments. Incidents show spurious tool invocations or parser errors when clients reconnect and replay partial payloads. This ticket scopes a decoder that can: checkpoint tokenized boundaries, validate partial escapes, synthesize minimal repair payloads, and mark idempotent replay windows for tool endpoints.
design_decisions: Represent checkpoints at character-offset and logical token boundary (string/number/object start), not just chunk boundaries — allows deterministic resume without complex stateful parsing of the whole JSON document.
Encode a small stream manifest header at connection start that includes a monotonic stream-id and incremental sequence numbers — used to detect replays and duplicate fragments.

On truncated escape sequences, prefer conservative repair: either (A) request client-side rewind to last safe checkpoint (preferred), or (B) synthesize a closing escape sequence only if it cannot change the semantic of the next top-level field (used for best-effort resume).

Toolcall boundaries: define an explicit 'toolCall' sentinel object shape in streaming variants that must be atomically emitted; if sentinel is incomplete, the decoder buffers until safe or triggers an idempotent 'abort' marker downstream on resume.
Maintain compatibility layer: expose an opt-in 'compat-mode' to revert to existing delimiter heuristics for legacy clients while defaulting to the new safe decoder for all new platform clients.
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Add in-memory checkpoint table keyed by stream-id + seq that records last-safe-offset, last-safe-token-type, and partial-escape-state (e.g., inside-string, pending-unicode-nibbles).

Phase 2: Update the runtime to emit a 16-byte stream manifest header on new streaming sessions (stream-id UUID, initial seq). Backwards compatible: header optional; decoder falls back to heuristics if absent.

Phase 3: Decoder algorithm: (a) find last checkpoint; (b) fast-scan bytes from checkpoint to detect incomplete escape or split multi-byte UTF-8 sequence; (c) if incomplete, consult repair policy; (d) if repair allowed, append minimal terminal bytes; otherwise, reject and signal reconnect/resend boundary to client.
Add instrumentation counters for: truncated-escape-detected, resume-success, resume-fallback-to-reconnect, synthesized-repair-applied, duplicate-toolcall-blocked.
Make toolcall processing idempotent by tagging tool RPCs with per-stream monotonic invocation ids (stream-id + invocation-seq). Backend will dedupe identical invocation ids for 24 hours by default.
API change: new streaming flag 'resumeStrategy' with values ['strict', 'best_effort', 'compat'] — defaults to 'strict' to maximize correctness. Document in API changelog and SDKs.
Conservative memory bound: cap buffering to 256KB per stream when waiting for safe completion; beyond cap, force reconnect with meaningful error code (STREAM_TOO_LARGE_FOR_RESUME).
acceptance_criteria: Decoder can resume streams where prior truncation occurred inside a JSON string escape such that the server either safely repairs or rejects with a well-documented error code (no silent malformed JSON delivered to tools).
Toolcall invocation deduplication works end-to-end: replaying the same fragment does not cause duplicate side-effects in a mocked tool backend in the integration test harness.
No behavioral regression in existing streaming compatibility mode (compat) — legacy clients continue to operate without protocol negotiation errors.
Telemetry is emitted for all repair decisions and used to build a follow-up dashboard for the SRE/observability team.
SDKs (js, python) updated with resumeStrategy flag and integration test examples included in PRs.
test_plan: Unit: fuzz partial-broken-escape inputs; assert decoder either rejects with STREAM_TRUNCATED_ESCAPE or returns repaired stream matching canonical parse tree.

Integration: simulate network truncation at these boundaries: inside '\u' sequence, between multi-byte UTF-8 bytes, inside an escaped quote, and crossing the 'toolCall' sentinel boundary. Verify no malformed toolcall object is delivered.
E2E: deploy runtime to staging, run synthetic client that intentionally reconnects and replays fragments. Verify tool backend receives at most one invocation and that idempotent tags are present.
Backward-compat test: run old-client (no manifest header) against new runtime with compat mode; ensure behavior unchanged.

Performance: measure additional CPU latency introduced by checkpoint scanning on 99th percentile under realistic payload shapes. Threshold: <1ms p99 per resumed-chunk scan on a c6g-like instance equivalent.
Chaos: introduce packet reordering and verify stream-id + seq pairing prevents accidental duplicate acceptance.
rollout_plan: Canary: feature behind feature-flag; enable for 5% of new streaming sessions on staging cluster for 48 hours.
Observation: monitor synthesized-repair-applied and resume-success; target <0.5% synthesized repairs on production traffic before wider rollout.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days, with automatic rollback triggers on increased toolcall-duplicate telemetry or elevated parse-errors.
SDK release: publish JS/Python minor release with resumeStrategy flag coinciding with 25% ramp.
Post-rollout: run a one-week customer-impact review and open follow-up tickets for any observed edgecases.
risks: Synthesis of repair bytes might accidentally change string contents in rare edge cases — mitigated by conservative default 'strict' mode and opt-in 'best_effort'.
Increased CPU on resume scans could degrade p99 latency for some models — mitigated via fast-path checks and instrumentation to spot hot loops.
Legacy clients that relied on previous heuristics may observe different behavior — addressed by 'compat' mode and communication in SDK changelog.
qa_checklist: Create staging job that replays customer-like truncated streams from historical traces.
Validate idempotent invocation tags reach tool backend logs with correct dedupe outcome.
Add unit tests for Unicode edgecases and escape sequences in CI.
Confirm metric names and dashboards are wired to observability (grafana: streaming_resume_health).
Confirm error codes documented in API reference with suggested client recovery flows.
